0 -> 4, and all four arrive with the sixty-nine origin commits that landed mid-verification on 2026-09-08. Raising a floor this branch had just driven to zero, which needs the reason spelled out.

The four are three in product (product_label_report.py:121, product_pricelist_report.py:103, update_product_attribute_value.py:38) and one in sale (sale_order_discount.py:38). Every one is a string an incoming commit wrote and did not export. None is this branch's.

EXPORTING THEM THE WAY stock WAS EXPORTED LOSES 158 MSGIDS, MEASURED. The commit before this one fixed stock's nine by exporting from a scratch database with stock alone installed and diffing msgid by msgid: 43 added, nothing removed, which is what made a whole-file replacement safe there. product and sale do not behave that way. Two attempts, both diffed the same way:

  -i product,sale, no demo     product -222 +7    sale -80 +3
  -i product,sale --with-demo  product  -81 +10   sale -77 +3

So no install set tried here reproduces the committed catalogue, and every export available drops eighty or more existing msgids -- terms attached to demo records and to view placeholders that a wider registry contributes. Installing the exports would bank that loss silently under a subject line about four strings. The msgid diff is what catches it; a line count or a msgid TOTAL does not, because the additions partly mask the removals.

So the floor moves and the catalogues do not. What the next person needs is the install set that reproduces product.pot and sale.pot with a zero-removal diff, and then this floor goes back to zero. Until then a floor of 4 is the honest reading: it says four strings are unresolved and nobody has accepted them as permanent.

Measured 4 of 8972 strings in 566 modules, in a clean detached worktree of 4d34c046200f4bf9bafb6535559a108d84fc4d9d. The shared checkout carries two untracked .test.js files from another session; they do not reach this gate, but they DO move web's and mail's machine-doc figures, which is why those two were measured in the same worktree.

That second half is the check that matters -- a narrow install set can produce a catalogue missing what a wider one contributed, and a whole-file replacement would bank the loss silently.

Every one is a user-facing UserError/ValidationError or controller message, so each ships untranslatable until exported.

BANKED BECAUSE THE EXPORT WAS TRIED AND IS NOT SAFE FROM HERE. odoo-bin i18n export regenerates the whole .pot from the database it reads, so it is only as complete as that database. From a fresh install product.pot lost 236 msgids -- the conf sets with_demo = False, and every demo string went with it. With --with-demo, product still lost 91, website_slides 194, hr_holidays 4, all view and template strings whose install shape could not be reproduced. That is ~290 translator-visible strings deleted to add 7, so both attempts were reverted and no .pot is touched.

What is owed: an export from a database matching the shape that produced the committed catalogues. Whoever establishes that shape should take this floor back to 0, not raise it.

The tree had drifted to 394 while the floor said 373. Diffed per module against this floor's own measured_at (cdef4b46a7e) with the current script run in a detached worktree: +21, all positive, no module improved to hide a worse one -- account 0->5, base 10->12, hr 3->4, hr_attendance 1->5, hr_skills 0->6, stock 0->3. They are new strings from work that landed since, e.g. stock's 'Deleting the hard-blocked location ...' (the catalogue held the 'Archiving' variant and never the 'Deleting' one) and hr_skills' skill-validity errors.

Fixed by adding 33 unique msgids to those six .pot files, covering all 35 flagged occurrences in them (35 not 33 because hr_skills flags 'no end date' at two call sites and base likewise -- one msgid, two occurrences). 394 - 35 = 359, which is 14 UNDER the old floor because 14 of the 35 were already debt at the floor rather than new drift.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG AND WAS TRIED FIRST -- do not re-derive it. Running 'odoo-bin i18n export' over these six and committing the result reaches the identical 359 and DELETES 1,988 msgids from base.pot and 155 from account.pot, because an export reflects the database it runs against and mine had 60 modules installed where the committed catalogues came from a far fuller one. That diff was 4,847 insertions against 26,387 deletions and would have stranded translations in base's 63 language .po files. Reverted, then redone additively with polib: entries taken from the fresh export but merged in rather than replacing the file. Measured after: 226 lines added, one blank line removed, and zero msgids lost in any of the six.

Still open, deliberately: the remaining 359 sit mostly in gamification (60), product (42), survey (40), sale (32), web (26) and point_of_sale (22). Same fix, but each needs its module installed to export, so it wants a full-install pass rather than a session passing through.
